newsitem.title: USA: Orange County assistant treasurer heads for trial.
newsitem.headline: Orange County assistant treasurer heads for trial.

text.p: The criminal trial of former Orange County assistant treasurer Matthew Raabe will get underway on Wednesday, more than two years after the county shocked Wall Street by declaring bankruptcy.
Jury selection for Raabe's trial is scheduled to begin in the morning in a Santa Ana courtroom. He is on trial for alleged crimes that contributed to the financial crisis.

Jury selection could last several days. Testimony is expected to begin on March 24, while the trial itself is expected to last through late April or early May, Deputy Orange County District Attorney Matthew Anderson said.
Raabe faces up to 12 years in state prison, Anderson said.
The county filed for bankruptcy in December, 1994, after sustaining losses of more than $1.6 billion on risky investments. The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
From March 1993 until he was placed on administrative leave in January 1995, Raabe was the assistant treasurer of the county. The county terminated his employment that March.
Raabe was indicted in May 1995 on several felony counts, including making untrue material statements in the sale of securities and misappropriation of public funds.
Raabe has denied any wrongdoing. His attorney was not immediately available to comment on Tuesday.
Raabe was one of several local officials facing charges following the bankruptcy.
In April 1995, former county treasurer Robert Citron pleaded guilty to six felonies for his role in the crisis.
A judge last November ordered him to spend a year in jail and pay a $100,000 fine, but Citron was later assigned to a community work programme in lieu of serving time in jail.
Last October, a judge sentenced former Orange County budget director Ronald Rubino to probation for charges stemming from the investment crisis.
The case against county auditor Steven Lewis has been put on hold by a state court pending a decision on his motion to recuse the district attorney.
